title: South Korea’s watchdog asks banks and insurers to report AI exposure
excerpt: South Korea's FSS has asked banks, brokerages and insurers to report AI investments and lending ties for the first time, Bloomberg reports.
content_html:
South Korea’s Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) has asked major banks, brokerages and insurers to report how much they have at stake in the AI industry, Bloomberg reported on Thursday. It is the first time the watchdog has asked.

The FSS is asking firms about direct and indirect investments in AI companies, as well as direct lending ties, Choi Bumjeon told Bloomberg. Choi heads the agency’s financial industry supervision team. Some firms have already responded, he said.

“As external concerns about hyperscalers and AI companies are mounting, the Financial Supervisory Service is assessing domestic financial firms’ exposure to AI as a precautionary measure,” Choi told Bloomberg.

TNW has not independently confirmed the survey with the FSS.

The move comes as investors and regulators watch AI spending more closely. Much of the money poured into the technology has been borrowed, Bloomberg noted.

South Korea is closely tied to the AI boom. It is home to memory chipmakers Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix. Its economy grew 1% in the third quarter, more than three times the Bank of Korea’s forecast, The Korea Times reported, as chip exports surged.

The FSS has also been watching how banks and insurers use AI. Earlier this year, it said it would draw up an AI risk framework for the sector. In April, Bloomberg reported that the FSS was reviewing the sectors it oversees for risks linked to overseas private credit.
